abstract: Introduction The choroid plexus (ChP), which produces cerebrospinal fluid and forms the blood-CSF barrier, has drawn growing interest in psychiatric and neurodegenerative neuroimaging. However, prior volumetric studies have relied largely on automated segmentation tools such as FreeSurfer, which show poor agreement with manual tracing, and have been limited to small, narrow-age, single-site samples. Methods We present DataPlex, a manually segmented lateral ventricle ChP dataset comprising 700 3T T1-weighted MRI scans drawn from 35 study/site categories, spanning a wide range of age, sex, and scanner manufacturer (GE, Philips, Siemens). Using generalized least squares models accounting for within-site dependence, we examined associations between ChP and lateral ventricle (LV) volume, and age, sex, scanner manufacturer, image resolution, a registration-based quality-control metric, intracranial volume, and cognitive performance. Results ChP volume displayed a positive linear association with age and was significantly greater in males than females, while LV volume showed a significant nonlinear relationship with age and no sex difference. Scanner manufacturer and image resolution were significantly associated with measured left LV volume but not with ChP volume, and the quality-control metric was not significantly associated with any outcome. Both ChP and LV volume were significantly associated with several cognitive domains, including emotion recognition, working memory, inhibitory control, and episodic memory. Conclusion These findings demonstrate meaningful differences in ChP volume across age and sex. DataPlex represents the largest demographically and technically diverse manually segmented ChP dataset to date, establishing reference benchmarks for future automated segmentation tools and underscoring the importance of accounting for demographic and technical covariates in choroid plexus research.

metadata.title: Age and Sex Differences in Lateral Ventricle Choroid Plexus Volume in a Large, Manually Segmented, Multi-Site MRI Dataset

summary: Manually segmented MRI dataset of 700 scans shows choroid plexus volume rises with age and is larger in males, with cognitive associations.
title: Age and Sex Differences in Lateral Ventricle Choroid Plexus Volume in a Large, Manually Segmented, Multi-Site MRI Dataset
